rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's grey depth is how strongly it promises to be checked — white means something inside promises nothing, deeper grey means stronger checks promised, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. Nothing here is green: green is kept for evidence a run has actually earned, and nothing has been run yet, so a picture full of promises should not look like a picture full of results. Hover anything for its meaning.

g.title: ply.yaml — the document this picture is drawn from. Everything you see here was declared in it; nothing was inferred from code. What each box has actually been checked for is what `cargo ply verify` reports, not this drawing.

What this document declares, before anything has been run. "0 functions promise nothing" counts functions with no checks against them at all -- code the diagram is showing you but says nothing about. Running `cargo ply verify` is what turns promises into results; this line never reports results.

component ledger — maps to Rust module ledger promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) hollow — declares nothing inside yet: no functions, no nested components. Nothing to zoom into; a sketch waiting for claims.

component withdrawal — maps to Rust module withdrawal pure — the double border is the seal: this component declares no capabilities and may not use any; capability use inside it is an error (A0408) declares checks up to fuzzed — checked against many random inputs — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet this box is this shade because `approve_withdrawal` is the weakest thing in it: it declares fuzzed — checked against many random inputs — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part
fee_cents bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times
total_debit_cents bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times
tier_fee_cents bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times

approve_withdrawal fuzz(256) — runs the function on 256 random inputs, checking the contract on each test — runs the declared examples plus generated inputs, checking the contract on each 2 worked example(s), each compiled into a test
withdraw bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times

withdrawal -> ledger — withdrawal may call ledger. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).
